display_title: 19-2-3 探究“天才儿童”是否存在

sentences.en: Let us start by looking at a modern ‘genius’, Maryam Mirzakhani, who died at the early age of 40.
sentences.zh: 先来看看一位现代“天才”玛丽亚姆·米尔扎哈尼。她年仅40岁就去世了。

sentences.en: She was the only woman to win the Fields Medal — the mathematical equivalent of a Nobel prize.
sentences.zh: 她是当时唯一获得菲尔兹奖的女性，这个奖在数学界的地位相当于诺贝尔奖。

sentences.en: It would be easy to assume that someone as special as Mirzakhani must have been one of those ‘gifted’ children, those who have an extraordinary ability in a specific sphere of activity or knowledge.
sentences.zh: 人们很容易想当然地认为，像米尔扎哈尼这样出众的人，小时候一定属于所谓的“天才儿童”，也就是在某一特定活动或知识领域拥有非凡能力的孩子。

sentences.en: But look closer and a different story emerges.
sentences.zh: 但仔细一看，就会发现事实另有一番模样。

sentences.en: Mirzakhani was born in Tehran, Iran.
sentences.zh: 米尔扎哈尼出生在伊朗德黑兰。

sentences.en: She went to a highly selective girls’ school but maths wasn’t her interest — reading was.
sentences.zh: 她就读于一所招生标准很高的女子学校，可她感兴趣的是阅读，而非数学。

sentences.en: She loved novels and would read anything she could lay her hands on.
sentences.zh: 她爱读小说，只要能弄到手的书，什么都读。

sentences.en: As for maths, she did rather poorly at it for the first couple of years in her middle school, but became interested when her elder brother told her about what he’d learned.
sentences.zh: 至于数学，她刚上中学的头两年学得不太好；后来哥哥给她讲起自己学到的东西，她才对数学产生了兴趣。

sentences.en: He shared a famous maths problem from a magazine that fascinated her — and she was hooked.
sentences.zh: 哥哥从一本杂志上找来一道有名的数学题与她分享，这道题深深吸引了她，她就此迷上了数学。

sentences.en: In adult life it is clear that she was curious, excited by what she did and also resolute in the face of setbacks.
sentences.zh: 成年后的她显然充满好奇心，对所做的事兴致勃勃，面对挫折也十分坚定。

sentences.en: One of her comments sums it up.
sentences.zh: 她自己的一番话概括了这一点。

sentences.en: ‘Of course, the most rewarding part is the “Aha” moment, the excitement of discovery and enjoyment of understanding something new . . .
sentences.zh: “当然，最有回报的是那个豁然开朗的时刻，是有所发现时的激动，也是弄懂新事物时的喜悦……

sentences.en: But most of the time, doing mathematics for me is like being on a long hike with no trail and no end in sight.’
sentences.zh: 可在大多数时候，做数学对我来说就像长途徒步：脚下没有路，眼前也看不到终点。”

sentences.en: That trail took her to the heights of original research into mathematics.
sentences.zh: 正是这条路把她带上了原创数学研究的高峰。

sentences.en: Is her background unusual?
sentences.zh: 她这样的成长经历很不寻常吗？

sentences.en: Apparently not.
sentences.zh: 看来并非如此。

sentences.en: Most Nobel prize winners were unexceptional in childhood.
sentences.zh: 大多数诺贝尔奖得主在童年时都没有什么出众之处。

sentences.en: Einstein was slow to talk as a baby.
sentences.zh: 爱因斯坦小时候开口说话很晚。

sentences.en: He failed the general part of the entry test to Zurich Polytechnic — though they let him in because of high physics and maths scores.
sentences.zh: 他没有通过苏黎世理工学院入学考试的综合部分，不过学校因为他物理和数学分数很高，还是录取了他。

sentences.en: He struggled at work initially, but he kept plugging away and eventually rewrote the laws of Newtonian mechanics with his theory of relativity.
sentences.zh: 他起初工作并不顺利，却始终埋头努力，最终用自己的相对论改写了牛顿力学定律。

sentences.en: There has been a considerable amount of research on high performance over the last century that suggests it goes way beyond tested intelligence.
sentences.zh: 过去一个世纪，大量关于高水平表现的研究都表明，这种表现远非智力测验的结果所能解释。

sentences.en: On top of that, research is clear that brains are flexible, new neural pathways can be created, and IQ isn’t fixed.
sentences.zh: 此外，研究还清楚地表明，大脑具有可塑性，新的神经通路可以形成，智商也并非一成不变。

sentences.en: For example, just because you can read stories with hundreds of pages at the age of five doesn’t mean you will still be ahead of your contemporaries in your teens.
sentences.zh: 比如，五岁就能读几百页长的故事，并不意味着到了青少年时期，你还会继续领先于同龄人。

sentences.en: While the jury is out on giftedness being innate and other factors potentially making the difference, what is certain is that the behaviours associated with high levels of performance are replicable and most can be taught — even traits such as curiosity.
sentences.zh: 天赋是否与生俱来、是否可能是其他因素造就了差异，这些问题尚无定论。但可以肯定的是，与高水平表现相关的行为是可以模仿再现的，其中大多数都能通过教导学会，甚至包括好奇心这样的特质。

sentences.en: According to my colleague Prof Deborah Eyre, with whom I’ve collaborated on the book Great Minds and How to Grow Them, the latest neuroscience and psychological research suggests most individuals can reach levels of performance associated in school with the gifted and talented.
sentences.zh: 我的同事德博拉·艾尔教授曾与我合著《卓越头脑及其培养》。据她介绍，最新的神经科学和心理学研究表明，大多数人都能达到学校通常认为只有天赋出众的学生才有的表现水平。

sentences.en: However, they must be taught the right attitudes and approaches to their learning and develop the attributes of high performers — curiosity, persistence and hard work, for example — an approach Eyre calls ‘high performance learning’.
sentences.zh: 不过，需要有人教给他们正确的学习态度和方法，他们也得培养出高水平学习者的特质，例如好奇、坚持和勤奋。艾尔把这种方法称为“高表现学习法”。

sentences.en: Critically, they need the right support in developing those approaches at home as well as at school.
sentences.zh: 重要的是，在培养这些学习方法时，他们在学校和家里都需要得到恰当的支持。

sentences.en: Prof Anders Ericsson, an eminent education psychologist at Florida State University, US, is the co-author of Peak: Secrets from the New Science of Expertise.
sentences.zh: 美国佛罗里达州立大学知名教育心理学家安德斯·埃里克森教授，是《刻意练习：如何从新手到大师》一书的合著者。

sentences.en: After research going back to 1980 into diverse achievements, from music to memory to sport, he doesn’t think unique and innate talents are at the heart of performance.
sentences.zh: 他从1980年起研究了音乐、记忆、体育等多种领域的成就，并不认为独一无二的先天才能是取得好成绩的核心。

sentences.en: Deliberate practice, that stretches you every step of the way, and around 10,000 hours of it, is what produces the goods.
sentences.zh: 真正带来成效的是刻意练习：每一步都挑战自己的能力，而且这样的练习要做约一万小时。

sentences.en: It’s not a magic number — the highest performers move on to doing a whole lot more, of course.
sentences.zh: 一万并不是什么神奇的数字；当然，最出色的人还会接着练习，练习量要大得多。

sentences.en: Ericsson’s memory research is particularly interesting because random students, trained in memory techniques for the study, went on to outperform others thought to have innately superior memories — those who you might call gifted.
sentences.zh: 埃里克森的记忆研究尤其有意思：研究中随机选出的学生接受了记忆技巧训练，后来表现超过了一些原本被认为记忆力天生更好、也许会被称为“有天赋”的人。

sentences.en: But it is perhaps the work of Benjamin Bloom, another distinguished American educationist working in the 1980s, that gives the most pause for thought.
sentences.zh: 不过，也许最值得人停下来思考的，是另一位美国杰出教育家本杰明·布卢姆在20世纪80年代所做的研究。

sentences.en: Bloom’s team looked at a group of extraordinarily high achieving people in disciplines as varied as ballet, swimming, piano, tennis, maths, sculpture and neurology.
sentences.zh: 布卢姆的团队研究了一批成就非凡的人，他们来自芭蕾、游泳、钢琴、网球、数学、雕塑和神经学等迥异的领域。

sentences.en: He found a pattern of parents encouraging and supporting their children, often in areas they enjoyed themselves.
sentences.zh: 他发现了一种共同模式：家长都鼓励、支持孩子，而且孩子所从事的往往也是家长自己喜爱的领域。

sentences.en: Bloom’s outstanding people had worked very hard and consistently at something they had become hooked on when at a young age, and their parents all emerged as having strong work ethics themselves.
sentences.zh: 布卢姆研究的这些杰出人士从小就迷上了某件事，而且一直为之刻苦努力。研究还发现，他们的父母自身也都十分敬业勤勉。

sentences.en: Eyre says we know how high performers learn.
sentences.zh: 艾尔说，我们知道表现卓越的人是怎样学习的。

sentences.en: From that she has developed a high performing learning approach.
sentences.zh: 她据此开发了一种培养卓越表现的学习方法。

sentences.en: She is working on this with a group of schools, both in Britain and abroad.
sentences.zh: 她正在与英国国内及海外的一批学校合作开展这项工作。

sentences.en: Some spin-off research, which looked in detail at 24 of the 3,000 children being studied who were succeeding despite difficult circumstances, found something remarkable.
sentences.zh: 一项由此衍生的研究详细考察了3000名研究对象中的24个孩子。他们虽身处困境却表现出色。这项研究有了一个引人注目的发现。

sentences.en: Half were getting free school meals because of poverty, more than half were living with a single parent, and four in five were living in disadvantaged areas.
sentences.zh: 其中一半因家境贫困而领取学校的免费餐食，一半以上生活在单亲家庭，五分之四住在条件较差的地区。

sentences.en: Interviews uncovered strong evidence of an adult or adults in the child’s life who valued and supported education, either in the immediate or extended family or in the child’s wider community.
sentences.zh: 访谈提供了有力证据：这些孩子的生活中有一位或多位重视并支持教育的成年人，可能是直系亲属或其他亲属，也可能来自孩子所在的更大社区。

sentences.en: Children talked about the need to work hard at school, to listen in class and keep trying.
sentences.zh: 孩子们谈到，应当在学校用功读书，在课堂上认真听讲，并且一直努力下去。

sentences.en: Let us end with Einstein, the epitome of a genius.
sentences.zh: 最后，让我们再来看看爱因斯坦这位典型的天才。

sentences.en: He clearly had curiosity, character and determination.
sentences.zh: 他显然既有好奇心，又有坚定的品格和决心。

sentences.en: He struggled against rejection in early life but was undeterred.
sentences.zh: 他早年曾努力面对种种拒绝，却没有因此打退堂鼓。

sentences.en: Did he think he was a genius or even gifted?
sentences.zh: 他认为自己是天才，或者哪怕只是有些天赋吗？

sentences.en: He once wrote: ‘It’s not that I’m so smart, it’s just that I stay with problems longer.
sentences.zh: 他曾写道：“我并没有多聪明，只是花了更长时间钻研问题。

sentences.en: Most people say it is the intellect which makes a great scientist.
sentences.zh: 大多数人认为，成就伟大科学家的是才智。

sentences.en: They are wrong: it is character.’
sentences.zh: 他们错了：靠的是品格。”
